Emend

/ih-MEND/ - rhymes with defend · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Emend means to correct errors in a written text.

The choir director emended the hand-copied hymnal, restoring the sharps a careless copyist had dropped.

Worked Example

Before the menus went out, the owner emended the printer's proof by hand: the 'sea brass' became sea bass again, and the fifteen-dollar soup returned to five.

Emend is correction with a scholar's precision — it fixes errors in a text so the words say what they were meant to say. You repair a roof, but you emend a hymnal, a caption, or a proof; the word almost never leaves the world of writing.

How Emend Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

correct

correct: the everyday word for fixing an error — emend is its bookish cousin, reserved for texts

edit

edit: to shape a text for length, clarity, or style — editing may change what emending would only repair

Antonyms

corrupt

corrupt: to introduce errors into a text — the scribe's sin that emending undoes

mangle

mangle: to garble a text until the meaning is lost

How Strong Is It? — proofread → emend → rewrite

proofread vs. emend

proofread vs. emend: Proofreading stops short of emending — a proofreader hunts and marks the errors; emending actually sets the words right.

rewrite vs. emend

rewrite vs. emend: Rewrite goes further than emend — an emended paragraph keeps its author's words with the faults repaired; a rewritten one starts over from a blank line.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of emend.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e-

Prefix — e-: out - a form of ex-

Root — mend

Root — mend: fault, blemish - Latin menda

Put it together

Put it together: E- (out) + menda (fault) = to take the faults out. Another disguise: emend looks like an en- word, but the n belongs to the root menda, 'a blemish.' Latin emendare traveled through French and wore down into the plain English verb mend — when you emend a page, you are mending it, one fault at a time.

Use the root in a new word: mend

Use the root in a new word: mend: By lamplight she mended the torn sail, and by morning no seam showed.

Root Check

Word Choice

scholarly

Emend belongs to editors, archivists, and anyone correcting a written text; outside writing, plain fix or correct is the natural choice. Keep it apart from its sound-alike cousin amend, which you met earlier in this course: laws, rules, and plans are amended — improved by change; manuscripts and misprints are emended — restored to what they should have said.
